steps.title: A tool call drawn in the parameter form is held by its grammar to each declared parameter once and every required one, so Qwen3.8 cannot draw a call the parser refuses and the chat route answers 500
steps.rationale:
Serves: the local worker's work on real steps. Two of the four steps it failed in loop-proof/local-demonstrated's run 2 ended at the server, not at the worker.

Disappears: a tool call the grammar lets the model draw and the parser then refuses. On ask-nothing/pointer, Qwen3.8 drew a call missing its required path, and the chat route answered 500 "inference: parse tool call 0: required function argument path is missing" (internal/inference/chat_parse.go:341). On vision-bridge/envelope-9b it gave path twice, and the route answered 500 "parameter path is duplicated" (chat_parse.go:439). Each 500 ended the worker's attempt: three attempts on ask-nothing/pointer in 30 s, and on envelope-9b after 119 calls.

The fix is where the call is drawn. The grammar a tool call is held to in the parameter form (<parameter=name>) admits each declared parameter at most once and every required one, in the declared order, so a call that would fail to parse cannot be drawn. The parser's refusals stay, for a call drawn with no grammar.

Check: TestAToolCallGrammarHoldsEachParameterOnceAndTheRequiredOnes compiles the grammar for a tool whose path is required and whose note is optional. It wants a call with path accepted, a call missing path refused, and a call giving path twice refused, read against the grammar's own acceptance. At base the grammar admits both bad calls.

steps.title: Every MP4 overgo writes is converted from RGB with BT.709 limited-range coefficients and tagged with its primaries, transfer, matrix and range, so a player shows the colours drawn
steps.rationale:
Serves: every clip a person is given; mp4-clips made MP4 the default.

Disappears: colours a player shifts. The MP4 writer pipes rgb24 to FFmpeg and asks for yuv420p with no colour options (internal/latentvideo/mp4.go start), so FFmpeg's scaler converts with its default BT.601 coefficients and writes no colour tags. A player shows untagged HD (a 3328 x 1920 finished clip, a 1664 x 960 one) as BT.709, so reds and greens shift; at 832 x 480 it is the player's guess.

The fix: convert with out_color_matrix=bt709 and out_range=tv, and tag -colorspace, -color_primaries and -color_trc bt709 with -color_range tv, for x264 and NVENC alike.

Check: TestAnMP4IsConvertedAndTaggedAsBT709 writes a frame of saturated patches through WriteClip. FFmpeg must report the stream as yuv420p(tv, bt709), and decoding it by its tags must return each patch within three 8-bit levels. At base the stream is untagged.

rtx-vsr/supplied builds on it: a supplied clip keeps its own tags through the same arguments.

steps.title: A finished frame is converted on the card to the 8-bit BT.709 YUV 4:2:0 FFmpeg encodes and handed to it as is, so the host reads an eighth of the bytes, keeps no float copy of the frame, and FFmpeg converts nothing
steps.rationale:
Serves: finished clips written faster and in less memory, the effect no longer waiting on the host.

Disappears: four host passes over every finished frame. Today a 3328 x 1920 frame comes back as 77 MB of float32 (finishingEncoder.add: MemcpyDtoH, then a loop rebuilding 19 million float32 values into a second 77 MB slice). The MP4 encoder then converts it value by value through a callback into 19 MB of rgb24, compares it pixel by pixel with bytes.Equal against a 19 MB copy of the frame before, and pipes it to FFmpeg, whose scaler converts it to YUV on the CPU. On rtx-vsr/nvenc's student clip, 81 frames finished at four times, the effect took 3.8 s of a 10.4 s write (7.8 frames a second), so about two thirds of the time is host work. Each stream holds about 197 MB of host buffers.

The fix: the effect already writes 8-bit RGBA on the card. NvCVImage_Transfer converts it there to BT.709 limited-range YUV 4:2:0 (8-bit RGB where the runtime writes no YUV), which is downloaded, 9.6 MB a frame at four times, and piped to FFmpeg as raw yuv420p tagged as clip-encode/colour-709 tags it. The float path stays for unfinished clips. ChangedPixels is counted on the bytes FFmpeg is handed, the change of what it counts named in the record.

Check: TestAFinishedFrameReachesTheEncoderAsEightBitYUV finishes the student clip at four times. The host must read width x height x 3/2 bytes a frame, the decoded frames must be within 40 dB PSNR of the float path's decoded frames, and two writes must be the same bytes. BenchmarkFinishedClipWrite (test-surface/judge-tests) gives frames a second and bytes allocated a frame, before and after, in the landing's message.

Predicted effect: about 16 frames a second at four times (the effect alone runs 21), and about 30 MB of host buffers a stream in place of 197 MB.

steps.title: A judged answer's cached probability is keyed by the right choice it scores, so a corrected answer is asked again and an unchanged one reused
steps.rationale:
Serves: SQA-343 (P2). Every judged reading that uses the judge's probability depends on it: soft TIFA, second-judge's rank agreement, rtx-vsr/judged-fidelity's comparison.

Disappears: a corrected answer scored by the probability of the old one. judgedAsked keys a cached answer by judge, code, environment, prompt, token limit and choices, but not the right choice. Its kept Probability is the probability of the answer accepted when it was asked. Correcting a case's answer from A to B therefore reuses 0.9 where the judge gave B 0.1.

The fix is the finding's own: the resolved right choice joins the existing key (rightChoice, shared with recordChoice). There is no new store; old entries stay and are no longer credited. Its two replay fixtures merge into TestSoftTIFAScoresTheProbabilityOfTheRightAnswer, keeping its numerical oracle.

steps.title: A judge opened in a process that holds a video model's sessions answers a picture within 1.5 times its time alone, the cause of the slowdown measured first and fixed where it lies
steps.rationale:
Serves: a server that holds a video model and a language model on one card, as overgo-server does. Measured in a test, but the cause lives in the shared code: a session director that never releases a session and a model loader that places what it is given.

Disappears: a language model slowed by a resident video model. On 2026-11-09 Qwen3.8-27B judged 192 pictures of 1024 x 960 in 2m49s in a process of its own. In the process that had just drawn 32 clips with the Wan student, whose sessions stay resident for the process's life (capabilityruntime's ModelSessionDirector has no release), it took about 20 s a picture. The card sat mostly idle with one host core busy, and 28 to 38 GB of the 48 were in use. The likely cause is the judge's layers placed on the host because the student's memory was counted (modelcli.ModelReserve, hybrid-native residency); contention is the other. The step measures which before changing anything.

The fix follows the cause. If placement: an idle media session gives its memory back when a language model would otherwise put layers on the host (an eviction on the director, the director's own lease rules kept). If contention: what contends is named and fixed there.

Check: TestAJudgeBesideAResidentVideoModelAnswersAtItsOwnSpeed draws 2 clips with the student and then judges 12 pictures in the same process. Each picture must take at most 1.5 times what the same pictures take in a child process with no video model. rtx-vsr/judged-fidelity then needs no child process.

steps.title: Landing scenarios share repeated build setup and merge duplicate walks while preserving isolated repositories and every failure and recovery assertion
steps.rationale:
Serves: every landing's wall, and the owner's direction of 2026-11-09 to use native Go testing to improve performance and drop unnecessary tests.

Disappears: repeated setup and duplicate scenario walks where the measurements identify them; the amount of wall time saved remains to be measured. Across the last fifteen landings the invariants stage took 2m21s to 3m18s, internal/landing 140 to 171 s of it, on every landing whatever it changed.

Evidence: go test ./internal/landing -count=1 -json on 2026-11-09 took 244 s for 80 tests. The twenty slowest are all parallel end-to-end landing scenarios at 103 to 201 s of wall each: TestTwoWorktreesLandThroughOneQueue 201 s, TestTrunkCheckoutFollowsWithItsOwnChangesKept 200 s, TestEveryStageFailureLeavesTheTrunkAlone 198 s, TestWorktreeCandidateIsIntegratedOntoTheTrunk 190 s, TestEveryRuleRefusalFixesOrPrintsItsEdit 181 s, and on. The serial tests sum to 43 s. Run side by side, the scenarios contend for the same cores, so their total, not any one of them, is the cost.

The step measures first, by stage of a scenario, where a scenario's time goes: the fixture repository, the tools it builds, the git and go commands it runs. The part every scenario repeats is then built once for the package (a fixture made once and copied per scenario, with Go's own test caching left to work), and scenarios that walk the same landing to different assertions are folded into subtests of one. The check named here holds the shared fixture. If the measurement finds the time elsewhere, the check is reset to what it finds before this step lands.

Predicted effect: less repeated setup and lower total package wall. The earlier under-one-minute package and 1m30s invariants figures are hypotheses, not timing assertions or acceptance limits. Retain isolated mutable repositories and each concurrency, failure, recovery and undo assertion, including the distinction between an assertion detecting removed behavior and a compile failure that supplies no undo evidence. Compare package wall and setup executions under equivalent conditions; do not add overlapping parallel test durations or count Go cache hits as new savings.

The model and objective here are the smallest that serve the purpose and are the owner's to change before the run: a person chooses what training starts from. Evidence limits: 300 cases is a proposed minimum, not a guarantee of power. Fix the detectable effect and uncertainty calculation for independent held-out units before exposure; correlated tokens or questions do not increase the independent sample count.
